researchQuestion: Can an independent semantic evidence assessor distinguish genuinely sufficient frozen retrieval evidence from plausible but irrelevant evidence better than the v3 deterministic score-and-language gate?
hypothesis: GPT-5.4 Mini will eliminate the deterministic assessor's false-positive evidence decisions while preserving at least 0.90 recall on canonically sufficient evidence states.
role: Offline component selection before any new end-to-end Agentic RAG integration.

labels.generalAnswerable: Sufficient only when at least one retrieved chunk matches frozen golden evidence.
labels.focusedComparativePositive: Sufficient only when canonical evidence for every expected technology side is present.
labels.modelVisibility: The assessor receives the original question and retrieved excerpts, never the expected label, golden answer, or accepted chunk ids.

singleChangedVariable: Deterministic score-and-language evidence assessment versus GPT-5.4 Mini semantic assessment on identical frozen retrieval states.

selectionRule.decision: Integrate the semantic assessor into a separately preregistered end-to-end Agentic RAG experiment only if every check passes. This experiment alone cannot enable production.

priorEvidence.v3Failure: The deterministic policy accepted three plausible but irrelevant general-negative retrievals and produced general FPR 0.1111.
priorEvidence.judgeCalibrationCaveat: GPT-5.4 Mini failed the ordinal generation-judge calibration but achieved 0.9375 binary pass agreement; this binary evidence-sufficiency task is separately evaluated rather than assumed valid.

limitations: Canonical-evidence labels may mark alternative but genuinely sufficient excerpts as insufficient.
The source states come from a validation trace already inspected during v3 diagnosis.
Selection qualifies a component for another validation experiment, not for production or locked-test execution.
